notes: M3-8 covers global packed bands. R5-6 already tracks the wider fix. R5-7 separately tracks cancelled encoders publishing unwritten bands.
summary: Tiled Clarity and packed Detail can reuse analysis of the wrong input after editing an already-enabled curve or changing Denoise.
evidence: The new curve LUT is uploaded independently of packed uniforms. Clarity coverage keys the uniforms, proxy epoch and Denoise controls, not the active global LUT or reconstruction variant. Global and local packed bands also omit actual Denoise identity and LUT contents. Global-to-local candidate keys omit effective global curve shape, and local curve offsets can stay fixed as shape changes.
proposed_fix: Use the effective upstream curve and resolved-input fingerprints for each cache. Fix separately from unsubmitted texture lifetime.
check: Repeat an active-curve move at 100% with Clarity only, then local Sharpen, and compare warm versus cold. Repeat Detail seeded with a primed Denoise ON/OFF pair and compare warm versus cold at fixed source and crop.

felt_impact: High candidate on Film-enabled Tone input: removing a substantial fraction of miss-path submits/work could save tens to hundreds of milliseconds end-to-end, unmeasured. Pan-only cache reuse benefits only coverage expansion.
summary: Post-lens Film controls can reuse the exact lens sum, but upstream Exposure or Contrast invalidates it and schedules 55 optical passes per rendered region.
evidence: The lens cache correctly includes the incoming grade. On miss the encoder extracts once and performs 27 horizontal and 27 accumulating vertical passes on the reduced spatial grid. Lens Strength can reuse the unmixed sum, but the other stages still run. Tone changes cannot reuse the old sum through nonlinear upstream grading. The tiled key also includes a whole-map coverage version for Clarity, so filling a distant map region can evict already-correct glow tiles.
proposed_fix: Keep real Tone dependencies. Profile the exact miss path before changing its dispatch organization. If pan misses are material, track local dependency or keep validated glow across coverage-only map growth where the sampled halo is already complete.
check: Film large Fit and 100%, paired exposure/contrast probes and own Lens Strength drag. Compare lens-glow reused=false/true, then run warm 100% pan with Detail Clarity active for the coverage case. Keep all fixed lens guards.

felt_impact: Likely below the 15 ms audit noise at a short radius; potentially tens of milliseconds of whole wait on a large view with a wide radius. Not measured.
summary: Halation extract and both broad blur passes run again even when only a downstream Film control changes.
evidence: The spatial function always writes extract, horizontal and vertical when Halation is enabled. The extract uses the pre-negative picture after lens and resolution scatter, plus physical radius/gate. Halation Amount and tint are applied only after the blur, and grain/print/scan controls are downstream. A Tone drag really changes this blur input; a downstream-only drag does not. The existing two ping-pong textures can be overwritten by lens work, and tiled scratch is reused between tiles.
proposed_fix: Measure first. Prototype an exact bounded pre-halation fingerprint and reuse the blurred alpha only for unchanged input, matching dimensions/grid, radius and halo. Prefer the current scratch allocation for a direct-only experiment; do not keep an unbounded tiled cache.
check: Film own Halation Amount and Grain Amount drags at large Fit and 100%; check smaller delta than upstream exposure/contrast only when blur is wide enough. Add a high-radius diagnostic if the default seed cannot resolve the cost. Compare finished pixels with the Film guards unchanged.

felt_impact: Two full-size passes and up to 16 bytes/pixel of Direct scratch are avoidable for Clarity-only. Expect tens of milliseconds on large processed views if the passes are a material share; unmeasured.
summary: Direct preview reruns both packed Detail blur passes even for a Clarity-only edit, and still does them when Clarity is the only enabled control.
evidence: Global graphActivity includes Clarity, and Direct unconditionally runs both packed-band passes whenever detailActive. Tiled global has the same unconditional pack/assemble path. The composite reads only the separate brightness map for Clarity. Texture-only and Sharpen-only likewise build all three packed components, rather than just their active components, though retained bands need explicit validity if a new component is enabled.
proposed_fix: Start with a true Clarity-only bypass for both routes and count scratch only when required. For combined controls, measure reuse of Direct bands on consumer-only amount/threshold drags and retain the current math and precision.
check: Detail own Clarity and Sharpen at large Fit and 100%. Add a Clarity-only diagnostic and compare against identical finished bytes after a cold render; exercise adding Texture/Sharpen before and after the bypass.

felt_impact: Highest Fit settle candidate: Nov 16 bounds combined grain cost at roughly 0.32–0.52 s on the cited grade, not a saving forecast for these two photos. A downstream-only cache could save a substantial fraction on a hit, zero when Tone changes the grain development input.
summary: Exact Fit Film recomputes its deterministic physical grain for every redrawn pixel, including on downstream-only edits.
evidence: Grain development depends on the pre-negative film input, coordinate, gate, seed and grain recipe. Exact reduced rendering can gather 16 sub-samples per pixel; native scale uses one, and interactive preview can use one. The field does not change randomly between frames. Nov 16 Neo evidence on a different saved grade puts finished 1024-edge waits at .405–.571 s with grain versus .054–.084 s without it. Exact density grain is not invariant under Tone but potentially invariant under downstream finishing changes.
proposed_fix: First profile exact stage and cache memory. Consider narrowly reusing an exact intermediate for scan/Lab controls or preserving reusable grain work only if current rounding and precision are preserved. Do not cache a static noise image in lieu of exposure-dependent grain; do not relax draft, export, Proof or parity requirements.
check: Film large Fit own Look/Grain and paired Tone/Denoise probes for exact grain load, then an own Scan Sharpening drag for potential downstream reuse. Compare at 100% as a native-scale control.

notes: Source trace, not visually reproduced. Phase 2 only permits findings file, so no patch was produced.
summary: At native zoom the tiled global Clarity prepass can fill too little source for later spatial effects, and can reduce wrongly clamped base-grade samples at chunk edges.
evidence: Map coverage starts at the pending tiles’ core bounds and expands only by Clarity reach. Lens/Halation/Structure and local Detail consume Clarity in the halo beyond the cores. Adding a long Film reach to a narrow Clarity map exposes samples whose map support was not filled. Separately the prepass computes base grade over exactly each reduction chunk, without an input guard for earlier BW and HSL neighbours; shader reads clamp at scratch bounds. roiSourceHalo takes a max of reach provisions rather than planning both these dependencies together.
proposed_fix: Plan coverage from the portion of Clarity output later passes read, and pad the source of each reduction chunk for BW/HSL/Denoise as required while writing only its interior texels. Share this plan with ROI source fetch and account for scratch.
check: At 100% compare cold ROI vs whole-frame tiled and warm pan-return with Clarity plus wide Lens/Halation. Separately test Clarity and active BW mix or HSL Shared Selection on chunk edges, versus fixed-resolution Direct and CPU. Keep all guards intact.

notes: Confirmed with a standalone Node arithmetic check at 8660×5784: the planner returns 272, while the shader’s leftmost read is −275. Not measured on GPU. Phase 2 only permits findings file, so no patch was produced.
summary: Halation’s tile halo omits bilinear sampling support when no Lens Filter is active.
evidence: At spatial grid 4, an interior tile’s first pixel x=0 relative to its core samples spatial texel -1 as well as 0. With a capped 64-texel blur, texel -1 needs extract texel -65. Its earliest integer extract sample is -259, and the capped 16-pixel edge detector reads -275. The Halation-only planner reserves 64*4+16=272, so the last needed neighbour clamps to the tile edge. The extra grid texel in the reach formula is reserved only for Lens, not for Halation’s own interpolation; with both stages active each reconstruction has its own support.
proposed_fix: Derive extraction and bilinear reach for every stage from its actual read coordinates and add the two reaches where chained, preserving existing physical caps.
check: Large 100% Film with Lens None, wide capped Halation, a synthetic bright edge aligned to the first or last few pixels of a tile; compare Direct vs Tiled with existing Film guards and repeat with Lens enabled.

felt_impact: Potentially large only near admission pressure or fallback. Expect negligible latency change with headroom, but 16 bytes per processed pixel of optional retained Direct scratch and bounded tile-cache residency are worth isolating. No measured memory bug.
summary: Detail scratch remains resident after bypass and its packed tile cache can compete with the native zoom working set.
evidence: At 50 MP, one RGBA16F texture is 400 MB. Direct would ask for four frame textures (1.6 GB) plus two Detail surfaces (800 MB), two quarter-grid Film surfaces (50 MB) and optional glow (25 MB), excluding source, presentation, caches and Clarity. Normal Full/100% admission is tiled or ROI, so those are not actual observed 100% allocations. Tiled scratch is halo-sized and reused; the 512² packed bands cost 2 MiB per cached tile and the 50 MP full-frame equivalent is ~400 MB per scope if untrimmed. Direct reuses and retains the Detail pair after a module-off draw; existing ceilings/eviction must be preserved. Tiled allocates six RGBA16F work surfaces including two Detail surfaces even for an inactive module, plus one source and optional denoised surface and spatial pair. At 512 with no halo a half-float source plus six surfaces is 14 MiB; a 272-pixel halo on each side with the same source and quarter grid pair costs ~61 MiB, excluding optional outputs and caches.
proposed_fix: Start by avoiding scratch for Clarity-only. If the ON-to-OFF idle footprint is material and route transitions reclaim too late, release optional Direct pairs under existing reclaim signals; preserve warm reuse when affordable. Measure active scopes and tile cache eviction separately.
check: Detail eye and paired Tone/Denoise probes at large Fit/100%; report route, processed edge, idle/peak allocator bytes, renderer/GPU physical footprint, and detail cache bytes. Compare ON to OFF in both orders.

felt_impact: One to three RGBA16F copies eliminated per rendered region. Likely few milliseconds at Fit, potentially tens at large viewport/catch-up. Lower priority than bad cache misses or grain.
summary: The Film chain schedules two full-size identity draws even on a simple no-structure frame.
evidence: filmResponseFragmentMain only textureLoads. encodeFilmChain first copies original into filmTexture before any neighborhood processing and finally copies scan output from filmTexture to finishTexture whenever structure is off or diagnostic-map mode is on. The lens-only branch adds another full-size identity draw after mixing. These copies preserve existing graph roles, but have no independent image math.
proposed_fix: Profile on device before changing graph roles. Experiment with passing the existing source view into the next stage and routing the last scan to the final target when it is not also an input. Retain all numerical store boundaries and strict comparisons.
check: Film eye and paired Exposure/Contrast Fit and 100%; instrument pass count and first feedback/settle versus same exact finished pixels. Include Film off, Lens only, diagnostic map, and Softness/Microcontrast on.

felt_impact: Avoids an entire redundant scheduled preview when open/unchanged close would otherwise reach encode, potentially one full graded frame of work. The existing debounce can coalesce short interactions, so there may be no noticeable gain on a single fast click.
summary: Film Stock picker focus is a real Grade preview, and focusing or closing on an unchanged option still retires and reschedules a frame.
evidence: There is no thumbnail job in this file: every focus calls choose, clones the entire opening recipe, and invalidates and debounces the active lane. The opening value still takes that path. restore unconditionally invalidates too. Unchanged focus/close and repeated focus of the same option can supersede in-flight work without any pixel change; a moving highlight may have to run Film exact if it settles. Cold selections may also await a full stock table fetch via renderToFrame; after load its packed stock slot is reused.
proposed_fix: Track the last applied option and whether any temporary recipe has changed. Skip invalidation for identical focus and untouched close. Preserve Escape restore, session/lane guards, forced retirement when pixels really changed, and one-entry undo.
check: Outside the standard matrix, profile own Film picker at Fit and 100% for open/close unchanged and rapid arrows then Escape. Count accepted and superseded renders; verify stock picker commit/cancel and history tests.

summary: Clarity’s retained GPU map allocations are missing from the resident memory ledger.
evidence: Each clarityMaps entry creates and retains three RG16F textures and only calls recordAllocation, which adds an instrumentation event when enabled, not an allocator reservation. resourceMemorySnapshot counts neither maps nor the separately captured surround textures. At 8660×5784 with base scale 4 the tiled map’s three textures account for about 37.6 MB before alignment; frame, analysis-frame, work and local scratch entries can coexist. This does not prove a ceiling violation.
proposed_fix: Budget persistent map growth under the existing memory limit and include live retained/deferred-release allocations exactly once in the allocator and diagnostics. Keep the current processing scale and memory ceilings.
check: Detail eye at large Fit and 100%, with Clarity on and with an anchor measuring in parallel. Compare map allocation events against gpuSnapshot bytes and physical footprint; verify cleanup at session reset and resize.

felt_impact: A clean miss already costs roughly 65 ms in isolated backend work, before parse/upload. Saving much of that could improve input-to-screen by tens of milliseconds or more on first-pass Print Contrast drags. Warm cache hits save little.
summary: Print Contrast sends megabytes of unchanged film tables for each newly sampled slider value, before the preview can draw.
evidence: The query key contains exact Contrast, Shadows and Highlights values; there are only eight variant slots. The backend caches a few computed curves but re-expands the base manifest, copies the full scanner table and serializes the entire payload for each uncached UI request. With Portra 400, exact contrast +20 and +24 emitted 4.38 MB of compact JSON each in a CPU-only spot check. Backend payload construction plus stdlib compact JSON serialization took about 65 ms each on this machine, excluding HTTP, renderer parse/pack/upload and GPU. renderToFrame awaits the stock request before drawing.
proposed_fix: Measure the drag. On a win, reuse the already-loaded immutable stock data and transfer only the variant print curve or legitimately changed scanner values. Preserve bytes and precision when packing the variant and leave delivery independent of transport optimization.
check: Add Film own Print Contrast at Fit and 100%, report cold and warm reruns separately, and break down request wait, payload size, GPU submission and first feedback/settle. Keep stock/paper/Lab qualification and fixed film/lens guards.

notes: Request poisoning and slot 0 reproduced without Electron. Visual and Proof effects are source-traced. Phase 2 only permits findings file, so no patch was produced.
summary: A single transient stock-table request failure can keep a selected Film stock visually missing for the rest of the frontend session.
evidence: Network errors, non-OK response codes and packing failures all enter the same permanent failed Set. Further requests for the exact key return early: slot remains 0, and the shader skips the measured response while other Film effects can continue. renderToFrame awaits a promise whose catch swallows the failure after logging, so it can present a frame without the named stock. This also applies to a single Print/Lab variant. Confirmed in a CPU-only Node stub: after one HTTP 503, requesting Portra Contrast +20 again makes no second fetch and slot() reports 0.
proposed_fix: Distinguish transient failures from permanent missing or invalid stock data. Retain a valid presentation or take the existing qualified fallback, and allow a bounded retry of transient table loads. Do not add UI or relax parity.
check: Use a fetch stub that fails once and succeeds, including a controlled Print variant. Verify no unqualified stock-less frame is accepted as exact and that the chosen look recovers. Audit existing Proof fallback if it shares this request.

summary: The current Detail audit changes pixels on both RAWs but is subtle at Fit and does not directly drag the radius cache path.
evidence: 1024-edge CPU-rendered HDR-to-SDR display RGB versus default, max-channel 8-bit delta: existing seed changes 62.16% of Canon IMG_7723.CR3 and 76.91% of Sony DSC00636.ARW pixels; 2.24% and 1.74% move by at least 3 codes. The proposed recipe gives 66.73% and 82.01% changed, with 9.06% and 7.28% moving by at least 3 codes. Clarity and Sharpen Amount are representative existing drags; neither samples the radius-dependent Clarity map blur in isolation.
proposed_fix: Seed Detail eye on, texture_amount=25, clarity_amount=50 (coefficient +0.40), clarity_radius_percent=0.75, sharpen_amount=50 (coefficient 0.50), sharpen_radius_px=0.8, sharpen_threshold=0, softness=0, microcontrast=0. Keep own Clarity and Sharpen drags and add Clarity Radius if the time budget permits; use a separate Clarity-only diagnostic for packed-band bypass, and a separate Softness or Microcontrast drag if measuring Film finishing.
check: H3/Phase 3 at Fit on both RAWs and at large 100%: validate live ON/OFF pixelsChanged and native slider events, including an own Clarity Radius drag. CPU spot-check is not GPU presentation or perceptual qualification.

summary: The Portra audit recipe makes a clear change on both RAWs, but current own drags miss the print-table path and the scan stage.
evidence: 1024-edge CPU-rendered HDR-to-SDR display versus default: existing recipe moves at least 3 max-channel RGB8 codes on 93.81% of Canon IMG_7723.CR3 and 76.08% of Sony DSC00636.ARW pixels; proposed recipe reaches 94.79% and 89.44%. Look Strength, Lens Strength, Halation Amount and Grain Amount are representative respective paths. They do not build controlled print tables, and default zero Scan Sharpening does not exercise its kernel. Direct recipe assignment does not run Film stock inheritance; these are resolved renderer values, not stock-relative UI percentages.
proposed_fix: Seed Film eye on with default resolved lane values plus film_stock=kodak_portra_400, look_strength=80, lens_filter=black_pro_mist, lens_strength=0.30, lens_size=1, halation_enabled=true, halation_amount=25, halation_radius=0.20, grain_enabled=true, grain_amount=28, film_resolution=90, print_contrast=20, scan_sharpening=25. Keep current own drags and prioritize Print Contrast. Add Scan Sharpening at 100%: on a sufficiently reduced Fit proxy the kernel rounds to radius zero.
check: H3/Phase 3 verify HDR-lane pixelsChanged at Fit on both RAWs and 100% on large; include own Print Contrast, plus Scan Sharpening at large 100% if budget allows. Use a separate capped-radius Halation check for edge correctness and wide-blur timing; do not make it the routine seed. CPU spot-check did not test live presentation.
